S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

info.persona: Yun Ha, a detail‑driven, art‑loving librarian who blends disciplined precision with a zest for community culture, balances meticulous budgeting with occasional indulgences, and they navigate health and fitness with proactive routines, all while managing a penchant for late‑night sketching and a stubborn skepticism toward unchecked trends.
info.professional_persona: Yun Ha, a seasoned library assistant clerk in Brooklyn, combines flawless cataloguing in Dewey Decimal and Library of Congress systems, meticulous metadata creation, and savvy use of OCLC WorldCat to guarantee data accuracy, while their disciplined, skeptical nature fuels relentless process improvements, and they champion community‑focused art programming.
info.cultural_background: Yun To Ha is a first‑generation Korean‑American who grew up in a bilingual household, speaking Korean at home and English in school. He retains deep ties to Korean cultural traditions, celebrating Lunar New Year and Chuseok with his family and preparing homemade kimchi and tteok. The Confucian values of discipline and respect for education inform his meticulous work ethic. Living in Brooklyn’s multicultural milieu, Yun integrates these roots with the city’s diverse artistic scene, often acting as a cultural bridge by introducing Korean art and literature to the library’s programming. His experience as an immigrant has fostered a strong appreciation for varied perspectives, while also shaping a healthy skepticism that drives his commitment to data accuracy and reliable service.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Yun’s curiosity fuels a vibrant set of hobbies. He frequently visits the Brooklyn Museum, MoMA, and local galleries, often sketching or photographing works that inspire him. He enjoys watercolor painting, reading art‑history books and contemporary Korean literature, and cooking traditional Korean dishes for friends. An avid believer in active living, he attends group Zumba classes, walks historic Brooklyn neighborhoods, and tends a small herb garden on his balcony. He plays chess at a nearby community center, participates in a multilingual book club, volunteers at cultural festivals, and is currently studying basic Japanese. Yun also maintains a personal blog where he shares library organization tips and reflections on art.
info.sports_persona: Yun Ha, an enthusiastic participant in weekly Zumba classes at a local community center, a regular member of the Prospect Park historic walking club, and a devoted fan of the Brooklyn Nets and New York Yankees, also joins a recreational bowling league at the Prospect Park Club during the winter months, and they relish the camaraderie of group fitness as much as the thrill of a close game.
info.arts_persona: Yun Ha, who spends weekends sketching masterpieces at the Brooklyn Museum and photographing installations at MoMA, creates delicate watercolors inspired by the works of Frida Kahlo and Mark Rothko, and they devote evenings to reading art‑history volumes and contemporary novels by Haruki Murakami and Han Kang, weaving these influences into curated library exhibitions.
info.travel_persona: Yun Ha, an avid traveler who has explored the historic streets of Kyoto, the bustling markets of Taipei, the art‑laden canals of Venice, and plans future trips to Barcelona’s modernist architecture and the seaside villages of Portugal, prefers carefully planned itineraries balanced with spontaneous discovery, and they often travel with a small group of friends to share cultural experiences.
info.culinary_persona: Yun Ha, a proficient home chef, delights in preparing homemade kimchi, spicy pork bulgogi, and sweet rice cake tteok for gatherings, while also experimenting with Mediterranean dishes like shakshuka, regularly harvests fresh basil and thyme from a balcony herb garden, and they enjoy pairing meals with fermented radish side dishes and a glass of plum wine.

info.persona: Jiaqi Wang channels analytical rigor into transformative process improvements while juggling a persistent worry habit and a zest for lively, collaborative experiences that keep both work and life in vibrant motion.
info.professional_persona: Jiaqi Wang, a 29‑year‑old lean‑manufacturing specialist, combines SAP and Oracle expertise, Six Sigma methodology, and bilingual communication with a pragmatic‑creative mindset, leading cross‑functional process‑improvement teams while energizing coworkers through their outgoing, group‑focused approach despite a penchant for worry‑driven over‑analysis.
info.cultural_background: Jiaqi is a second‑generation Chinese American. Her parents emigrated from Guangdong before she was born, and she grew up in a bicultural household where Mandarin was spoken at home and English at school. She observes traditional holidays such as Chinese New Year and the Mid‑Autumn Festival, and she maintains close ties to the local Chinese community in Chicago’s Chinatown. Her upbringing blended Confucian values—respect for elders, diligence, and collective harmony—with the individualistic, entrepreneurial spirit of the Midwest, giving her a flexible worldview that informs both her personal life and professional decision‑making.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Jiaqi enjoys energetic group fitness like spin classes and Zumba, which satisfy her outgoing nature and help manage stress. She is an avid cook, especially experimenting with modern twists on traditional Chinese dishes, and often hosts dinner gatherings for friends. On weekends she hikes the nearby Moraine Hills, practices landscape photography, and participates in a local book club focused on contemporary fiction and philosophy. She also volunteers at a community theater, engages in Spanish language‑exchange meet‑ups, and attends improv comedy workshops to keep her creative spark alive.
info.sports_persona: Jiaqi Wang fuels their high‑energy routine by attending spin classes at CycleFit, Zumba at RhythmMotion, hiking the nearby Moraine Hills each weekend, cheering for the Chicago Bulls, Chicago Cubs, and Chicago Bears, and training with the Chicago Trail Runners club for long‑distance runs.
info.arts_persona: Jiaqi Wang volunteers as a stagehand at the community theater, sharpens quick wit at The Second City improv workshops, participates in a book club that discusses contemporary fiction by Haruki Murakami and philosophy of Slavoj Žižek, and draws creative inspiration from musicians like Mitski, cellist Yo‑Yo Ma, and comedian Awkwafina, while they constantly seek fresh perspectives for personal projects.
info.travel_persona: Jiaqi Wang blends spontaneous weekend road trips with carefully planned overseas adventures, having trekked the ancient streets of Kyoto, marveled at Barcelona’s Gaudí masterpieces, explored the Canadian Rockies, and now dreaming of Patagonia’s Torres del Paine while they balance travel expenses with a savings plan for future consultancy work.
info.culinary_persona: Jiaqi Wang’s culinary repertoire features modern twists on heritage flavors, such as Sichuan‑peppercorn‑infused dumplings paired with smoked tofu, miso‑glazed salmon with bok choy and yuzu, and maple‑roasted duck served alongside lotus‑root slaw, showcasing their confident home‑chef skills and a love for bold, aromatic ingredients.

info.persona: Andre Moreira is a detail-oriented yet creatively restless tech-music enthusiast who juggles spreadsheets and guitar solos, tends to over-budget on studio gear, and they harbor a healthy dose of skepticism that fuels their competitive edge.
info.professional_persona: Andre Moreira, a 31-year-old aspiring digital media project manager in Nashville, merges their Python data-analysis expertise, meticulous budgeting experience, and Pro Tools audio-editing skill to coordinate tech-music projects, applying the practical curiosity that they bring and the disciplined organization they maintain while allowing enough flexibility to improvise during spontaneous jam sessions.
info.cultural_background: Andre was raised in a historically Black neighborhood of Nashville, where family gatherings centered around gospel music, church fellowship at an African Methodist Episcopal congregation, and the preparation of soul‑food meals. The city's rich musical heritage—blending country, R&B, and blues—has shaped his appreciation for rhythm and storytelling. He is deeply aware of the civil‑rights legacy in Nashville and values the resilience of the Black community, drawing inspiration from its traditions of collective support, oral history, and creative expression. These cultural influences inform his identity, his artistic pursuits, and his desire to give back to the community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Andre enjoys playing guitar and experimenting with digital audio production, often crafting beats and mixing tracks at home. He is an avid reader of nonfiction, focusing on history, technology, and social justice topics. Andre frequently hikes the trails around Percy Warner Park and likes to cook Southern comfort dishes, especially soul‑food recipes passed down through his family. He also plays chess, participates in small jam sessions with local musicians, and volunteers at a community center where he tutors youth in basic computer skills.
info.sports_persona: Andre Moreira spends weekends hiking the trails of Percy Warner Park with the Nashville Trailblazers hiking club, runs occasional 5K races during spring, and follows the Nashville Predators, Tennessee Titans, and Nashville SC for their sports fandom, often streaming games after a long day of coding, though they sometimes skip a workout when work pressures mount.
info.arts_persona: Andre Moreira channels their artistic side by playing guitar in small jam sessions that cover Jimi Hendrix and modern soul artists like D'Angelo and Erykah Badu, attends intimate performances at Nashville’s Bluebird Café, and draws inspiration from visual artists such as Kehinde Wiley and cinematographer Ava DuVernay, while they remain reserved about sharing their own compositions publicly.
info.travel_persona: Andre Moreira prefers meticulously planned road trips, having driven to New Orleans for its music scene and to Asheville for mountain hikes, while dreaming of a future adventure to Iceland’s glaciers and Japan’s Kyoto temples, balancing their love of cultural immersion with budget-conscious itineraries, and they often draft travel spreadsheets the night before departure.
info.culinary_persona: Andre Moreira is an intermediate home cook who masters Southern comfort dishes like fried chicken, collard greens, and cornbread, seasoning them with smoked paprika, hot sauce, and a dash of cayenne, and they love pairing their meals with craft beers from local Nashville breweries, even though they occasionally over-salt a dish in the rush of a jam session.
